Subject: Packaging for pilot -> production: need clarity on upgrade triggers

We're getting internal alignment for a 6-week pilot focused on triage automation. A few questions came up from procurement and engineering that I wanted to capture in one place so we can lock the pilot order: 

- We expect burst peaks to ~40 concurrent requests with 256-token average output. For the pilot, are we best to start on a dedicated small pool (2x A100 equiv) or the compact hosted tier? What are the tradeoffs for predictable burst vs. unit cost?
- If pilot metrics hit the threshold you recommended (90th p95 latency < 180ms and 15% lower per-token cost vs hosted baseline), what's the smoothest path to convert to production? Can we do a seat/feature swap without re-onboarding?
- Our procurement team asked about staged discounts for conversion (pilot -> prod Year 1). Do you offer a pilot conversion credit or an early-conversion discount?

We're trying to put a recommended procurement flow together this week. Can you share a short doc or a few concrete plan options (pilot SKU, expected token buckets, 30/60/90 day upgrade triggers, and any conversion credit mechanics)?

Appreciate it — Maya

Hi Maya — great to hear the demo resonated. I put together three pragmatic options below and attached a one-pager plus a pilot metrics template to make procurement's life easier (attached: AsterPilot_SKU_Options_v1.pdf, pilot-metrics-template.csv).

Quick summary (pilot -> prod paths):

1) Host-to-Prod (Lowest friction)
   - Start: Hosted compact tier (metered) with a reserved concurrency bucket for the pilot (burst cap).
   - Pros: Fast start, no infra onboarding, pay-as-you-go.
   - Cons: Less predictable latency at peak unless we reserve extra burst capacity.
   - Upgrade path: Convert metered usage into a 6-month committed capacity contract. We apply a pilot-conversion credit up to 20% of pilot spending (applies to Year 1 invoice).

2) Dedicated Pilot Pool (Predictable performance)
   - Start: Dedicated small pool (2x vA100-equivalent), limited to your pilot scope for isolation and consistent p95 latency.
   - Pros: Predictable latency and KV cache warm-up, easier compliance handoffs.
   - Cons: Higher base cost during pilot.
   - Upgrade path: Increase pool size or move to multi-pool prod. Pilot credits: we provide a 10% discount on the first 3 months of committed Dedicated capacity if you convert within 45 days of pilot end.

3) Hybrid (Pilot caching + Hosted fallback)
   - Start: Dedicated cache layer (prefix/KV) + hosted model serving for overflow. Good if you have cold-start sensitive flows.
   - Pros: Best balance of cost and p95 protection; incremental scale.
   - Upgrade path: Flip hosted overflow to dedicated as traffic grows; credits prorated based on reserved months.

Upgrade triggers we recommend (we put these directly in the attachment template):
- Conversion trigger A: sustained 14-day 95th pctl latency < 200ms AND monthly token consumption > 1.2x pilot forecast.
- Conversion trigger B: production readiness checklist complete (SLA, SSO, billing contacts, audit log retention).
- Financial trigger: forecasted 6-month spend > $100k -> reserved capacity recommended.

Discount mechanics and terms (summary):
- Pilot-conversion credit applies as a one-time invoice credit against the first prod invoice. Cap: 20% of accumulated pilot spend (hosted path) or up to 10% of first committed monthly Dedicated spend (dedicated path).
- Early-conversion discount: convert within 30 days of pilot end to unlock an additional 5% off Year 1 for deals > $150k ARR.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll drop the one-pager + template (attached). Ben can run a quick sizing check against your estimated concurrency and token profile — Ben, can you confirm the recommended pool sizing for 40 concurrent, 256-token avg?
- Maya/procurement: fill the metrics template during pilot so we have objective triggers to convert.
- If you want legal/finance engagement, loop in Aster Health Legal and our pricing ops team; I can introduce them after you pick a preferred path.

Best,

Thanks — good questions. Short answers here, and we'll produce a one-page sample invoice tomorrow morning.

- Pilot-conversion credit: credits are applied to invoices and are non-refundable (they do not get paid out). They reduce the first prod invoice(s) until exhausted.
- Dedicated minimum on conversion: standard is monthly billing with a 3-month minimum on the initial committed block when converting from a dedicated pilot. We can flex to monthly with purchase order language for enterprise procurement but need AP/finance contact in advance.
- Stacking discounts: we can combine a pilot credit + an early-conversion Year 1 discount, but the total effective discount is capped at 25% for deals under $200k ARR. For your example (committed $18k/mo), you would be eligible for pilot credit (applied to first invoice) plus an early-convert 5–10% Year 1 discount depending on final term; I'll show both scenarios in the sample.

Ben — can you run the sizing + sample invoice calc for the committed $18k/mo scenario? Lauren — please prepare a short note on the on/offboarding steps for the Dedicated pool so Aster's security folks know the sequence.

I'll follow up with the sample invoice and a short AMP-style decision table (pilot path vs prod path) by EOD tomorrow.
